value: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (2023). Regulatory Impact Analysis of the Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources: Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review. EPA-452/R-23-013, December 2023. Research Triangle Park, NC: Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards.

Targeted pass on the 278-page RIA. Page numbers are printed page numbers (chapter-page, e.g. 4-75). The RIA does NOT reproduce the model plant control cost tables (those are in the Nov 2021, Dec 2022 and 2023 Final Rule TSDs, which are not held), so only three cost sets exist: Table 4-21 (p.4-75), average capital cost and annual operating cost per affected unit by segment and source, 2019 USD; flare capital 100,579 and annual 25,000 with 95% control (p.2-55); and control levels (95% for storage vessels and wet seals, 29%/36% for liquids unloading, p.2-51, 2-55). Costs are relative to a baseline without the rule, so capex is negative for two rows and opex negative where gas recovery revenue appears to be included (not stated). No methane avoided per unit is printed, so no capacity rows; national methane reductions by source (Table 5-5), present-value costs (Table 5-6), counts of affected units for 2030 (Tables 2-6 to 2-8) and gas prices are in other-values, from which a per-unit methane figure could be approximated by the coordinator (not done here: counts are incremental by year). Source defects: the text on p.4-74 calls Table 4-21 values median but the table is titled average; wet-seal centrifugal opex of 25,000 equals the flare annual cost. Not extracted: benefits chapters, market and small-entity analysis, environmental justice, regulatory alternatives (Table 2-14/2-15, Chapter 5 other options), all non-GHG material.
